legacy_root.title: Contract: Append-only event schema with causality and redaction rules
legacy_root.question: Specify the event record: monotonic sequence, timestamp with timezone, actor, unit id, phase, state transition, correlation and causality ids, payload, and redaction rules for secrets and personal paths. Define the append-only enforcement mechanism (what makes an in-place edit detectable) and the ordering guarantee when events arrive from parallel substrates.
legacy_root.answer: The event record is one JSON object per JSONL line with monotonic per-writer seq, timezone-stamped ts, actor, unit_id, phase, from_state/to_state, correlation_id, causality_id, payload, and a redactions array. Secrets are rejected at write time (fail closed; the planted canary ARC0086-CANARY-SECRET must never appear in durable bytes). Personal home paths are redacted to [REDACTED:personal-path] before the line is appended. Append-only is enforced by a hash chain: sha256 = SHA256(prev_sha256 || LF || canonical body). An in-place edit of a historical line breaks the chain at that record even when the line count is unchanged. Parallel substrates do not share a global seq and must not be totally ordered by wall-clock ts; the authoritative order is happens-before via causality_id. Concurrent events remain unordered. Live EVENTS.jsonl on this worktree is present (406 bytes, 2 parsed, 0 parse-failures, 2 schema-gaps, 0 bad-records). The production writer tools/command-center/close.py:append_event is a schema gap relative to this contract (no chain, no redaction, different shape). SUCCESS:ARC-0086

ts.description: RFC3339 / ISO-8601 datetime with explicit timezone.

causality_id.description: Parent event_id this record happens-after, or 'genesis'.

seq.constraint: >=1, monotonic per writer_id in the durable file
seq.why: A global integer across parallel substrates is a lie: two writers cannot allocate it without a lock. Per-writer seq is the local monotonic counter; file order is the hash chain.

ts.constraint: ISO-8601 / RFC3339 with explicit timezone; naive rejected
ts.why: A timestamp without a timezone is not an instant.

unit_id.constraint: work-unit id or NONE for non-unit ledger events

state_transition.constraint: both non-empty; same-state allowed for notes

correlation_id.constraint: groups one run / conversation; not a parent pointer

causality_id.constraint: parent event_id this record happens-after, or genesis

payload.constraint: after write-time redaction; secrets never persist

redactions.constraint: one row per personal-path substitution applied at write

integrity.prev_sha256: GENESIS (64 zero hex) for the first record, else prior sha256
integrity.sha256: sha256(prev_sha256 + LF + canonical JSON of body without chain fields)

redaction_rules.why_reject_secrets: A redacted secret still means the writer received recoverable secret material and might have logged it on a failed path. Refuse the write; durable bytes stay unchanged.
redaction_rules.why_redact_paths: Home directories leak operator identity. Substitute the home prefix; keep the relative suffix for operational debugging.
redaction_rules.aligns_with_ADV-0045: Append-only wins for historical log bytes. Erasure of new personal content is write-time minimisation / redaction, not an in-place rewrite.

append_only_enforcement.writer_opens: append-mode only; never seek-back, truncate, or rewrite
append_only_enforcement.status_ledger_note: status_ledger.py is absent. The contracted verifier is command-center/p2-wave/probes/ARC-0086/eventlog.py:verify_chain. Do not claim a second digest implementation that is not on disk.
what_breaks_the_chain: rewrite of any hashed field on a historical line
insertion of a line that does not bind the prior sha256
truncation that drops a chain link
append_only_enforcement.torn_tail: An incomplete last line is a bad-record, not a schema-gap. Repair truncates to the last valid link and reports loss (CC-0007); it must not hide the tear.
append_only_enforcement.byte_prefix: A legal append extends the file; the historical prefix bytes are unchanged. Prefix-hash (CNF-0049) and hash-chain are both required: prefix-hash catches rewrite, chain names the record.

parallel_substrate_ordering.file_order: Durable append order as serialized by the filesystem; recorded by the hash chain. This is what landed, not what the clocks said.
parallel_substrate_ordering.guarantee: If A happens-before B (B.causality_id reaches A.event_id), any valid causal replay lists A before B. Concurrent events (no path either way) remain unordered; a reader must not invent a total order from ts. Clock skew across substrates is expected.

legacy_writer.note: Current production writer does not emit the ARC-0086 record. The sample was taken on an isolated tempfile, never live EVENTS.jsonl. Migrating close.py is CC-0007 / a follow-on implementation unit; this unit freezes the contract.

legacy_root.evidence_requirement: The schema is validated against the existing EVENTS.jsonl by parsing every line; the parse-failure count is reported and each failure is classified as a schema gap or a bad record.

tests_required.requirement: Append-only control: modify one historical line and assert the integrity check detects it
Redaction control: a record carrying a canary secret must be rejected or redacted at write time, proven with a planted canary

docs_code_divergence.note: The contract is frozen. The production writer remains the unchained, unredacted JSONL append measured by ADV-0045 and CNF-0049. Closing the gap is not this unit.

residual_unknowns.claim: Independent cross-vendor reviewer of this leftover envelope has not been dispatched.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Dispatch a fresh-context reviewer over the catalog output_path after schema-valid write.
